theme: Injection and unsafe input handling in a small Node.js + TypeScript document search and export API

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The search term from the request is interpolated inside a quoted ILIKE literal of the SQL text handed to node-postgres. A term containing a quote closes the literal and appends arbitrary SQL (`x%' UNION SELECT ... --`); nothing is bound as a parameter.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The owner filter taken from the query string is interpolated into the text of a knex `raw` statement. `raw` executes the string as given, so the value becomes SQL; knex only parameterises values passed as bindings.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The public unsubscribe endpoint copies `email` and `token` out of the JSON body without checking that they are strings and uses them as a MongoDB filter. A body of `{"email": {"$ne": ""}, "token": {"$ne": ""}}` matches an arbitrary subscription, so anyone can unsubscribe recipients without knowing their tokens (operator injection).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The export format chosen by the caller is spliced into a command line run by `child_process.exec`, i.e. by `/bin/sh -c`. The request schema only requires a non-empty string, so `pdf; curl ...` or `$( ... )` runs as the service account.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The attachment file name from the route is joined onto the storage root and read with no containment check. `path.join` normalises `..` segments, so an encoded `..%2F..%2F` name resolves outside the root and any file the process can read is returned.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The import preview fetches whatever URL the caller supplies, from inside the network, and returns its status, content type and size: cloud metadata endpoints, loopback admin ports and internal hosts are all reachable. The schema checks only that the value parses as an http(s) URL.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Uploaded metadata XML is parsed by libxml with entity substitution switched on (`noent: true`). A document declaring `<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` has the file's contents substituted into the field the service stores and returns.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Uploaded report layouts are loaded with a YAML schema that re-registers the `!!js/function` tag the YAML library removed for safety: the tag's scalar is compiled into a function. A layout's formatter is called while rendering, so an uploaded layout runs arbitrary JavaScript in the service.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Computed-column formulas from a caller's report definition are executed with `vm.runInNewContext`. The vm module is not a security boundary (`this.constructor.constructor('return process')()` escapes it), so a formula runs arbitrary code in the service process.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A saved search's filter expression, written by the caller, is compiled with `new Function` into the predicate applied to results. The expression is arbitrary JavaScript and runs with the service's privileges.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The recursive merge used to apply a PATCH body to the caller's stored preferences copies every own key, including `__proto__` (an own property of objects produced by JSON.parse). Descending into it reaches Object.prototype, so a body of `{"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}}` adds a property to every object in the process.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The search widget endpoint returns `text/html` that echoes the raw query string. The archive front end inserts the widget into its page, so `q=` runs script in that page for anyone who follows a crafted link.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The browser client reads the title and description out of a user-supplied XML document with `textContent` (which decodes entities) and interpolates them into an `innerHTML` template, inside a quoted attribute and as element text. The document's author controls both, so `" onmouseover="...` or `` runs script in the reader's session.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: After a share link is unlocked the handler redirects to the `next` query parameter as given. `next=https://attacker.example/login` sends a user who trusted the archive's link to any site.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The highlight endpoint compiles a caller-supplied regular expression and runs it over whole documents. JavaScript's backtracking engine has no match timeout, so `(a+)+$` against a long run of `a` blocks the event loop and with it every request the process serves.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Export audit records are written as plain text lines, one per export, including the download file name chosen by the caller. A name containing a newline ends the record and forges further audit lines that are indistinguishable from real ones.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Share-link passwords are stored as an unsalted MD5 hex digest. MD5 is fast and unsalted, so a leaked table is reversed with precomputed tables or GPU guessing in seconds per password.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Every successful delivery logs the subscriber's e-mail address. Logs are shipped and retained outside the subscription store's retention and erasure controls, so the address outlives an unsubscribe.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The subscriber's e-mail address is placed in the query string of a GET to the CRM. URLs are written verbatim to access logs of every proxy and server on the way, outside the CRM's own data controls.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The browser client keeps the e-mail addresses of recent report recipients in localStorage. They persist after sign-out and are readable by any script running on the origin.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The exported flattener walks an uploaded JSON metadata document by recursing into every nested object and array with no depth limit. JSON.parse accepts nesting far deeper than the call stack, so a request body of about ten kilobytes of nested brackets exhausts the stack (RangeError) and fails the import.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: node-postgres query with a `$1` placeholder and the value passed in the values array: the value never becomes SQL text.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An ORDER BY clause is built by interpolation, but both holes come from code: a column name from a fixed lookup table keyed by an enum the request schema enforces, and one of two direction literals.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: knex `raw` with `?` placeholders and the values in the bindings array: knex sends them as parameters.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: MongoDB lookup by e-mail address, but the body was parsed by a schema that accepts only a string for the address: an operator object cannot reach the filter.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `execFile` with a configured binary, no shell, and every value its own argument; the size comes from a fixed table keyed by an enum and both paths are generated by the service.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The template name is resolved against the root and the result must start with the root plus a path separator before it is read: `..`, absolute paths and sibling directories with a common prefix are all refused.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The feed URL comes from the request, but it is fetched only if it is https and its host is on the configured partner allowlist (exact match), with redirects refused.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: libxml parse with its defaults: entity substitution and DTD loading are off, so external entities are never loaded or expanded.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The partner feed is parsed with fast-xml-parser, a JavaScript parser that does not resolve external entities or fetch DTDs.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Uploaded column mappings are loaded with the YAML library's default schema, which has no tags that construct functions or class instances: the result is plain data, and it is then validated by a schema.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A sort comparator is compiled with `new Function`, but every fragment of its source comes from code: a column accessor taken from a fixed table keyed by an enum value, and one of two direction literals.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Layout overrides from the request are merged into a prototype-less object, key by key, after `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` are refused and only known keys are accepted.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Document cards are rendered by a template engine with auto-escaping on: every value from the database is HTML-escaped on output.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Titles read from the documents are passed through an HTML escaper before they enter the innerHTML template.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The redirect target from the query string is used only if it is a same-origin path (one leading slash, no second slash or backslash, no scheme); anything else goes to a fixed page.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A RegExp is built from the caller's search term, but every metacharacter is escaped first, so the pattern is a literal string match and cannot backtrack catastrophically.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A constant, anchored pattern with no nested or overlapping quantifiers, applied to a length-limited value.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: MD5 as an HTTP ETag for cache validation of document cards. No security property depends on it: a collision would only make a cache revalidate wrongly for content the caller may already read.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Download passwords for export bundles are hashed with bcrypt at cost 12 and verified with bcrypt's own compare.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The caller-chosen file name is logged as a field of a structured JSON record; the serializer escapes control characters, so a newline cannot start a new record.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A bounce is logged with a keyed HMAC of the address, not the address: a stable pseudonymous reference that cannot be reversed without the key.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `email=true` is a channel switch on an opaque subscription id; no personal data is in the URL.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: localStorage holds the page size and theme only; nothing personal or secret.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A recursive walk over a caller-supplied filter tree, but it carries its depth and refuses a tree deeper than a small fixed limit before recursing.

entries.rationale: Certified free of the injection, unsafe-input, weak-hash, personal-data-leak and uncapped-recursion concepts this repository measures (whole file).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Promoted from a scanner false positive (iteration 1). Authorization rules are named and listable: the scopes are constants in one module, every /api route declares its scope with requireScope at registration, and the README lists the scope per endpoint. A rule that wants a named policy set finds one here.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: No directory access: nothing builds an LDAP filter.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: No XPath evaluation: XML is read by walking the parsed tree, never by expression.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: No binary formats are read: every input is JSON, YAML, XML or text, and no length field from an input sizes an allocation.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Every route parses its input with a schema, so validation exists, but the schemas check shape only: the fields that reach SQL, a shell, the file system, outbound requests, regular expressions and redirects are unconstrained, and two routes skip validation. Read as the web-security posture as a whole, headers and transport are good while MD5 password storage and personal data in an outbound URL pull it down. Middling.
